elements: Coordinate frame drawn as three thin black lines with small cone arrowheads meeting at an origin behind the lower-left of the solid: z axis rising at the upper left (label 'z' at its tip), y axis extending to the right (label 'y'), x axis coming forward toward the lower left (label 'x')
Closed solid E: pale blue semi-transparent body shaped like a rectangular prism whose six faces bulge outward and whose twelve edges are rounded, long dimension running left-to-right along y
Boundary surface S: the visible bulging shell of E, with darker blue curves tracing the rounded corner seams
Dashed blue curves marking the hidden rear vertical edge and the hidden rear/bottom seams of the solid
Italic label 'E' at the middle of the solid, on the front face
Italic label 'S' just outside the upper-right corner of the solid, naming the boundary surface

Seven short dark-blue outward normal arrows, each with an italic bold 'N' at its tip: two rising from the top face, two dropping from the bottom face, one from the left (−y) face pointing left, one from the right (+y) face pointing right, and one on the upper surface angling up and back

Long unlabeled orange arrows of the ambient vector field F, drawn parallel from lower-left to upper-right, three passing through the solid and four passing outside it (above-left, above-right, below-left, below-right)
On-screen readout panel reporting the selected patch's F·N sign, the running net flux across S, and the total divergence integral over E

interactions.teaches: That E is a genuine closed solid and S is its full boundary — rotating reveals the rear faces whose normals also point away from the interior, so no part of S is missing from the flux count.

That flux is decided locally by the angle between F and N: clicking a face patch brightens its N and the orange arrows crossing it, and reports F·N as positive where the field exits, negative where it enters, near zero where it grazes.

That a uniform field (strength 0, exactly the figure as drawn) has zero divergence and therefore zero NET flux — the positive contributions on the top and right faces are cancelled by the negative ones on the bottom and left. Increasing the source term splays the orange arrows outward, makes div F positive everywhere, and makes every face contribute positively.
interactions.label: Source strength s in F = u + s·(r − r₀)

interactions.teaches: That the same number can be read two ways: as the outward flux summed over the boundary S, or as the divergence accumulated throughout the interior of E.

demo_steps.title: The solid E and its boundary S
demo_steps.narration: The pale blue solid is E; its bulging shell is the closed surface S. Every short dark blue arrow N is a unit normal pointing out of E, never into it — that outward choice is what fixes the sign of the flux.

demo_steps.title: Face by face with a uniform field
demo_steps.narration: The long orange arrows all point the same way, lower-left to upper-right. Click the top and right patches: F·N is positive, the field leaves E. Click the bottom and left patches: F·N is negative, the field enters.

demo_steps.title: Uniform means no net outflow
demo_steps.narration: Whatever flows in through the lower-left faces flows straight out through the upper-right ones. The net flux across S is zero — and a constant field has divergence zero, so the triple integral over E is zero too.

demo_steps.title: Add a source
demo_steps.narration: Raising s bends the orange arrows outward from the centre of E. Now F·N is positive on every patch of S, so the outward flux grows — the surface is genuinely losing field.

demo_steps.title: The divergence theorem
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the interior view: the solid shades by div F = 3s, constant throughout. Its integral 3s·Vol(E) matches the flux totalled over S — the boundary sum and the interior sum are the same number.

plan.geometry_notes: Axis convention matches the drawing: +Y is screen-right (the 'y' axis), +Z is screen-up (the 'z' axis), +X comes forward toward the lower-left (the 'x' axis). Solid E is centred at r₀ = (0, 0.3, 0.2) and measures X 2.2 (depth) × Y 4.0 (the long horizontal dimension) × Z 1.8 (height); all six faces bulge outward ~0.18 and the twelve edges are rounded, radius ~0.25 — build as a superellipsoid |x/1.1|^4 + |(y−0.3)/2.0|^4 + |(z−0.2)/0.9|^4 = 1. Volume ≈ 14.5 world units (use the mesh's computed volume for the readout). Axes originate just behind the lower-left corner of the solid at about (0.6, −2.6, −1.2): z runs up 3.2, y runs right 4.8, x runs forward 3.0; thin black #111 lines, cone heads, italic serif tip labels. Hidden rear vertical edge and rear bottom/left seams drawn as light dashed blue #5b8fc0 curves. Colours: solid fill pale steel blue #b3c9de at 0.55 opacity, seam curves #2f6193; normal arrows dark navy #1f4e79, length ~0.9, shaft radius 0.035, italic bold 'N' at each tip; field arrows orange #e8622a, length ~2.4, shaft radius 0.04. FIELD FORMULA: F(r) = u + s·(r − r₀) with fixed unit direction u ≈ (0.20, 0.80, 0.56) normalised and s = sourceStrength; therefore div F = 3s (exactly 0 at the default s = 0) and the flux across S = 3s·Vol(E). Do not shade any interior divergence at s = 0 — it is identically zero, and the net flux readout must show 0 there. Field arrows sit on a loose 3×3 lattice offset in x and z so three thread through the solid and four pass outside (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right); at s = 0 they are exactly parallel as in the source figure, and they fan outward as s rises. Label positions: italic 'E' on the front face centre near (1.1, 0.1, 0.25); italic 'S' just outside the top-right corner near (0.4, 2.6, 1.6). Normal placements: top face at y ≈ −1.2 and y ≈ +1.1 pointing +Z; one more on the top face near (0.3, 0.3, top) tilted up-and-back toward (0.5, 0.2, 0.85); one on the −Y face pointing −Y; one on the +Y face pointing +Y; two under the bottom face at y ≈ −0.3 and y ≈ +0.9 pointing −Z. Sign of F·N at s = 0: +Y face and top face positive, −Y face and bottom face negative, +X front face slightly positive, −X back face slightly negative — and the signed areas cancel to zero overall.
plan.notes: Build E as a superellipsoid mesh (SphereGeometry vertices remapped by the exponent-4 formula) with MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent 0.55, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide; add only the twelve rounded corner seams as extracted TubeGeometry/Line curves rather than a full wireframe. Hidden rear seams as LineDashedMaterial with depthTest false so they read through the body. Normals and field arrows as grouped CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head so individual arrows can be recoloured. Labels ('x','y','z','E','S','N') as CSS2D/sprite italic serif text that always faces the camera. Click picking: invisible spherical-cap raycast proxies over each of the six face regions; on hit, tint that patch, brighten its N arrow to #0d3a63, brighten the 2–3 orange arrows nearest it to #ff7a3c, dim the rest to 0.25 opacity, and print F·N with its sign. Slider s: recompute every orange arrow's direction and length from F(r) each frame and keep the shared readout of net flux = 3s·Vol(E) and ∭div F dV = 3s·Vol(E) in sync so the two always agree. Toggle 'Divergence inside E': fade normals and exterior arrows to 0.15 and shade the interior with nested translucent iso-shells or a point cloud whose brightness is proportional to 3s — completely uncoloured when s = 0. OrbitControls with damping, target at the solid centre, clamped min/max distance.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a single three-dimensional diagram of a closed surface carrying outward normal vectors. A pale blue solid shaped like a rectangular prism with bulging faces and rounded edges occupies the center, set in a frame whose z axis rises at the upper left, y axis extends right, and x axis comes forward to the lower left. The letter E labels the solid at its middle and the letter S labels the boundary near its upper right. Short dark blue arrows, each labeled N, project outward from the boundary: two from the top, two from the bottom, one from the left face, one from the right face, and one drawn on the upper surface angling up and back. Longer unlabeled orange arrows run in parallel through and around the figure from lower left to upper right, standing for the ambient vector field. Dashed curves mark the hidden rear edges. Setting the labeled normals against the uniformly directed field arrows shows at a glance how much of the field crosses the boundary at each face. The diagram accompanies a result tying the flux of a vector field across a closed surface to a triple integral of its divergence over the solid inside.
authoredInteractions:
- Click for each face region of S: the learner selects a patch of the closed surface and the outward normal N and nearby orange field arrows brighten, making clear when the field contributes positive, negative, or little flux through that patch.
- Toggle between boundary-flux and enclosed-volume views: the learner switches emphasis from arrows crossing S to shading inside E, making clear that the divergence theorem equates surface flux with accumulation of divergence throughout the solid.
authoredContext:
Let S be a piecewise, smooth closed surface that encloses solid E in space. Assume that S is oriented outward, and let F be a vector field with continuous partial derivatives on an open region containing E (the figure). Then

The divergence theorem follows the general pattern of these other theorems. If we think of divergence as a derivative of sorts, then the divergence theorem relates a triple integral of derivative divF over a solid to a flux integral of F over the boundary of the solid. More specifically, the divergence theorem relates a flux integral of vector field F over a closed surface S to a triple integral of the divergence of F over the solid enclosed by S.

The divergence theorem relates a flux integral across a closed surface S to a triple integral over solid E enclosed by the surface.

A diagram of a closed surface S, vector field, and solid E enclosed by the surface in three dimensions. The surface is a roughly rectangular prism with curved sides. The normal vectors stretch out and away from the surface. The arrows have negative x components and positive y and z components.

Recall that the flux form of Green’s theorem states that ∬DdivFdA=∫CF·Nds. Therefore, the divergence theorem is a version of Green’s theorem in one higher dimension.

demo_steps.title: The closed surface S bounding E
demo_steps.narration: The pale blue solid E is enclosed by the surface S. Short dark blue arrows N stick out of every face, always pointing away from the interior.

demo_steps.title: Where the field exits and enters
demo_steps.narration: The orange arrows form a uniform field running lower-left to upper-right. Click the right and top patches — F·N is positive there, so the field leaves E. On the left and bottom patches F·N is negative: the field enters.

demo_steps.title: Accumulation inside the solid
demo_steps.narration: Switching emphasis to E fades the boundary arrows and shades the interior by divergence. Net outflow across S equals the total divergence piled up inside — the divergence theorem.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World axes match the figure: +Y is screen-right (the 'y' axis), +Z is screen-up (the 'z' axis), +X comes forward toward the lower-left (the 'x' axis). Solid E is centered at approximately (0, 0.3, 0.2) and measures about X 2.2 (depth) × Y 4.0 (length, the long horizontal dimension) × Z 1.8 (height); all six faces bulge outward by ~0.18 and the twelve edges are rounded with radius ~0.25 (build as a superellipsoid/rounded box, e.g. |x/a|^4+|y/b|^4+|z/c|^4=1). Axes: z from 0 up to 3.2, y from 0 right to 4.8, x forward to 3.0, each thin black (#111) with a cone arrowhead and italic serif label at the tip. The origin sits just behind the lower-left corner of the solid so the axes pass near/through the solid's left rear; the hidden rear vertical edge and the hidden bottom edges are drawn as light dashed blue (#5b8fc0) curves. Colors: solid fill pale steel blue #b3c9de at ~0.55 opacity with darker blue seam/edge curves #2f6193; normal arrows dark navy #1f4e79, length ~0.9, shaft 0.035 radius, each with an italic bold 'N' label at the tip; field arrows orange #e8622a, length ~2.4, shaft 0.04, all parallel with unit direction ≈ (0.20, 0.80, 0.56) (normalized) i.e. rising to the upper right; arrows arranged on a loose 3×3 lattice offset in x and z so three pass through the solid and four pass outside it (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right). Labels: 'E' italic at the front face center near (1.1, 0.1, 0.25); 'S' italic just outside the top-right corner near (0.4, 2.6, 1.6). Normal placements: two on the top face at y≈-1.2 and y≈+1.1 pointing +Z; one on the top face near (0.3, 0.3, top) angled up-and-back toward (0.5,0.2,0.85); one on the −Y face pointing −Y; one on the +Y face pointing +Y; two on the bottom face (y≈-0.3 and y≈+0.9) pointing −Z. Flux sign per patch with this field: +Y face and top face positive, −Y face and bottom face negative, +X (front) face slightly positive, −X (back) face slightly negative.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the solid as a superellipsoid mesh (SphereGeometry vertices remapped, or a rounded-box with bulge displacement) using MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent opacity 0.55, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide, plus a matching darker-blue wireframe of only the 12 rounded corner seams (extract via curves, not full wireframe). Hidden rear edges as LineDashedMaterial lines that are drawn with depthTest disabled so they read as dashes through the body. Normals and field arrows as ArrowHelper-style groups (CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head) so individual arrows can be recolored on click. Labels ('x','y','z','E','S','N') as sprite/CSS2D italic serif text that always faces the camera. Click picking: attach invisible raycast proxy patches (slightly offset spherical caps) to each of the six face regions; on selection set that face's patch to a highlight tint, brighten its N arrow to #0d3a63, brighten the 2-3 nearest orange arrows to #ff7a3c and dim all others to 0.25 opacity, and display an F·N sign readout. Toggle: 'Boundary flux' state shows full-opacity normals and arrows with the shell edges emphasized; 'Divergence inside E' state fades the normals and exterior arrows to 0.15, raises solid opacity, and renders an interior scalar shading (nested translucent iso-shells or a point cloud colored by div F) to suggest accumulation. Keep OrbitControls with damping, target at the solid center, no zoom-to-extremes (min/max distance clamp).

discrepancies: Orange field arrows are rendered nearly parallel to the view direction, so they appear short and foreshortened with the cone heads seen end-on (small blobs); in the source they are long, clearly diagonal (lower-left to upper-right) arrows with visible arrowheads spanning well past the solid.

The solid E reads as a soft pillow/superellipsoid; the source shows a distinctly box-like rounded solid with pronounced straight edges, visible top/side faces and strong solid + dashed seam curves (the dashed hidden edges are barely perceptible here).
Overall scene scale is small relative to the canvas — the solid occupies a modest fraction of the frame, while the source fills most of the figure, making seams, N arrows and E/S labels less legible.

The interior 'N' arrow shown in the source penetrating the solid (pointing down-left through E) and the paired top angled N are only loosely reproduced; the arrangement of the nine normals does not match the source layout closely.

Interior point cloud and nested shells (divergence emphasis mode) are additions not present in the source, and with a strictly uniform field they imply nonzero divergence, which is conceptually shaky.
evaluation.notes: A recognizable, well-labeled 3D reproduction of the divergence-theorem figure with rich, functional interactions (face picking with F·N readout, emphasis toggle, guided steps); main weaknesses are foreshortened/short orange field arrows, an over-rounded solid with faint seams, small overall scale, and an added interior 'divergence accumulation' visualization that conflicts with the uniform field.

feedback.rationale: The critic flags hallucinated content (interior point cloud/nested shells implying nonzero divergence for a uniform field) plus a mismatched normal-vector arrangement, indicating the interaction plan itself includes conceptually wrong elements that must be removed/restructured before implementation polish.

The x-axis is far shorter and thinner than in the source, and its cone head renders as a small dark blob at the lower-left rather than a clean arrow extending well forward of the solid.
The solid reads as a grey/steel mass rather than the source's pale translucent cornflower-blue body; the interior dashed hidden edges are consequently less visible than in the printed figure.

Closed solid E: pale blue semi-transparent body shaped like a rectangular prism whose six faces bulge outward and whose twelve edges are rounded, long dimension running left-to-right along y
Boundary surface S: the visible bulging shell of E, with darker blue curves tracing the rounded corner seams

Italic label 'E' at the middle of the solid, on the front face
Italic label 'S' just outside the upper-right corner of the solid, naming the boundary surface

Seven short dark-blue outward normal arrows, each with an italic bold 'N' at its tip: two rising from the top face, two dropping from the bottom face, one from the left (−y) face pointing left, one from the right (+y) face pointing right, and one on the upper surface angling up and back

Long unlabeled orange arrows of the ambient vector field F, drawn parallel from lower-left to upper-right, three passing through the solid and four passing outside it (above-left, above-right, below-left, below-right)
On-screen readout panel reporting the selected patch's F·N sign, the running net flux across S, and the total divergence integral over E

interactions.teaches: That E is a genuine closed solid and S is its full boundary — rotating reveals the rear faces whose normals also point away from the interior, so no part of S is missing from the flux count.

That flux is decided locally by the angle between F and N: clicking a face patch brightens its N and the orange arrows crossing it, and reports F·N as positive where the field exits, negative where it enters, near zero where it grazes.

That a uniform field (strength 0, exactly the figure as drawn) has zero divergence and therefore zero NET flux — the positive contributions on the top and right faces are cancelled by the negative ones on the bottom and left. Increasing the source term splays the orange arrows outward, makes div F positive everywhere, and makes every face contribute positively.

demo_steps.title: The solid E and its boundary S
demo_steps.narration: The pale blue solid is E; its bulging shell is the closed surface S. Every short dark blue arrow N is a unit normal pointing out of E, never into it — that outward choice is what fixes the sign of the flux.

demo_steps.title: Face by face with a uniform field
demo_steps.narration: The long orange arrows all point the same way, lower-left to upper-right. Click the top and right patches: F·N is positive, the field leaves E. Click the bottom and left patches: F·N is negative, the field enters.

demo_steps.title: Uniform means no net outflow
demo_steps.narration: Whatever flows in through the lower-left faces flows straight out through the upper-right ones. The net flux across S is zero — and a constant field has divergence zero, so the triple integral over E is zero too.

demo_steps.title: Add a source
demo_steps.narration: Raising s bends the orange arrows outward from the centre of E. Now F·N is positive on every patch of S, so the outward flux grows — the surface is genuinely losing field.

demo_steps.title: The divergence theorem
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the interior view: the solid shades by div F = 3s, constant throughout. Its integral 3s·Vol(E) matches the flux totalled over S — the boundary sum and the interior sum are the same number.

plan.geometry_notes: Axis convention matches the drawing: +Y is screen-right (the 'y' axis), +Z is screen-up (the 'z' axis), +X comes forward toward the lower-left (the 'x' axis). Solid E is centred at r₀ = (0, 0.3, 0.2) and measures X 2.2 (depth) × Y 4.0 (the long horizontal dimension) × Z 1.8 (height); all six faces bulge outward ~0.18 and the twelve edges are rounded, radius ~0.25 — build as a superellipsoid |x/1.1|^4 + |(y−0.3)/2.0|^4 + |(z−0.2)/0.9|^4 = 1. Volume ≈ 14.5 world units (use the mesh's computed volume for the readout). Axes originate just behind the lower-left corner of the solid at about (0.6, −2.6, −1.2): z runs up 3.2, y runs right 4.8, x runs forward 3.0; thin black #111 lines, cone heads, italic serif tip labels. Hidden rear vertical edge and rear bottom/left seams drawn as light dashed blue #5b8fc0 curves. Colours: solid fill pale steel blue #b3c9de at 0.55 opacity, seam curves #2f6193; normal arrows dark navy #1f4e79, length ~0.9, shaft radius 0.035, italic bold 'N' at each tip; field arrows orange #e8622a, length ~2.4, shaft radius 0.04. FIELD FORMULA: F(r) = u + s·(r − r₀) with fixed unit direction u ≈ (0.20, 0.80, 0.56) normalised and s = sourceStrength; therefore div F = 3s (exactly 0 at the default s = 0) and the flux across S = 3s·Vol(E). Do not shade any interior divergence at s = 0 — it is identically zero, and the net flux readout must show 0 there. Field arrows sit on a loose 3×3 lattice offset in x and z so three thread through the solid and four pass outside (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right); at s = 0 they are exactly parallel as in the source figure, and they fan outward as s rises. Label positions: italic 'E' on the front face centre near (1.1, 0.1, 0.25); italic 'S' just outside the top-right corner near (0.4, 2.6, 1.6). Normal placements: top face at y ≈ −1.2 and y ≈ +1.1 pointing +Z; one more on the top face near (0.3, 0.3, top) tilted up-and-back toward (0.5, 0.2, 0.85); one on the −Y face pointing −Y; one on the +Y face pointing +Y; two under the bottom face at y ≈ −0.3 and y ≈ +0.9 pointing −Z. Sign of F·N at s = 0: +Y face and top face positive, −Y face and bottom face negative, +X front face slightly positive, −X back face slightly negative — and the signed areas cancel to zero overall.
plan.notes: Build E as a superellipsoid mesh (SphereGeometry vertices remapped by the exponent-4 formula) with MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent 0.55, depthWrite false, side DoubleSide; add only the twelve rounded corner seams as extracted TubeGeometry/Line curves rather than a full wireframe. Hidden rear seams as LineDashedMaterial with depthTest false so they read through the body. Normals and field arrows as grouped CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head so individual arrows can be recoloured. Labels ('x','y','z','E','S','N') as CSS2D/sprite italic serif text that always faces the camera. Click picking: invisible spherical-cap raycast proxies over each of the six face regions; on hit, tint that patch, brighten its N arrow to #0d3a63, brighten the 2–3 orange arrows nearest it to #ff7a3c, dim the rest to 0.25 opacity, and print F·N with its sign. Slider s: recompute every orange arrow's direction and length from F(r) each frame and keep the shared readout of net flux = 3s·Vol(E) and ∭div F dV = 3s·Vol(E) in sync so the two always agree. Toggle 'Divergence inside E': fade normals and exterior arrows to 0.15 and shade the interior with nested translucent iso-shells or a point cloud whose brightness is proportional to 3s — completely uncoloured when s = 0. OrbitControls with damping, target at the solid centre, clamped min/max distance.
